title: optimize-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion-kvcache-batching
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Reduce serving cost and end-to-end latency for quantized models (INT8/FP8) by fusing dequantization with main kernels, folding SmoothQuant adjustments into the quant pipeline, and improving scheduling/KV-cache locality for continuous batching. This PR implements a set of kernel- and runtime-level optimizations to close the gap between our quantized paths and the FP32 baseline.

What changed (single-run summary):
- Added fused dequant+matmul kernels (int8/ fp8 aware) that avoid an extra memory write pass for common attention and FFN matmuls.
- Folded SmoothQuant scaling into the quantize->dequant pipeline so per-channel scales are applied during compute, removing redundant tensor ops.
- Introduced an FP8 fast-path for attention QKV projection & output GEMMs for models that use GEMM-friendly layouts.
- Improved KV-cache memory layout and lookup to prioritize hot entries and reduce page movements under continuous batching workloads.
- Adjusted scheduler affinity to increase reuse of per-request KV cache slices across microbatches, reducing serialization points.
- Added microbatch coalescing heuristics in the continuous batching layer to favor larger in-flight batches when latency SLOs allow.
- Extended unit tests and added end-to-end throughput/latency bench harnesses for INT8/FP8 paths.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement fused kernels and pipeline changes
- [x] Add unit tests covering per-channel scales + smoothquant folding
- [x] Add microbench harness and compare against baseline
- [x] Run cluster-scale integration (k8s) smoke tests
- [x] Performance review + signoff

Commits (high-level):
- "fused: add dequant+gemm kernels for int8/fp8" (core/runtime/kernel_impl.cc, kernel_dispatch.h)
- "quant: fold smoothquant into quantize/dequant path" (runtime/quant/transform.cc)
- "kvcache: hot-slice layout + lookup optimization" (runtime/kvcache/layout.h, scheduler/placement.cc)
- "batching: continuous batching coalescing heuristics" (runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cc)
- "tests: add int8/fp8 e2e bench harness" (bench/quant_bench.cc)

Files touched (high level):
- core/runtime/kernel_impl.cc
- core/runtime/kernel_impl.h
- core/runtime/kernel_dispatch.h
- runtime/quant/transform.cc
- runtime/quant/quant_utils.h
- runtime/kvcache/layout.h
- runtime/kvcache/lookup.cc
- runtime/scheduler/placement.cc
- runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cc
- bench/quant_bench.cc
- tests/quant/quant_fusion_tests.cc
- build/CMakeLists.txt (small hook for new bench executable)

Small snippets (illustrative, not full diffs):
- Fused kernel registration (kernel_dispatch.h): "register_kernel(FusedDequantGemm, KernelKey::INT8 | KernelKey::FP8);"
- SmoothQuant fold (quant/transform.cc): "apply_scale_in_gemm = true; // avoids separate scale tensor op"
- KV lookup (kvcache/lookup.cc): "if (hot_slice) return fast_path_fetch(hot_slice);"

Benchmarks (representative):
- Model: t5-large-like encoder-decoder, 512 tokens, batch size 8, continuous ingestion profile
- Baseline (previous INT8 path): throughput 1.0x, p99 latency 420ms, token-server cost index 1.0
- This PR INT8 fused: throughput 1.8x, p99 latency 380ms (-9.5%), token-server cost index 0.65 (-35%)
- FP8 fast-path (where applicable): throughput 2.6x, p99 latency 360ms (-14%), token-server cost index 0.52 (-48%)
- KV-cache locality changes: observed 10-18% reduction in membrane/page faults in long-lived sessions under continuous batching
- Microbatch coalescing: average CPU overhead for batching down from 12% to 6% while keeping 95th latency within SLO

Compatibility and safety: 
- All changes gated behind runtime flags: "enable_quant_fusion" and "enable_fp8_fastpath" (disabled by default in canary clusters).
- Falls back to existing dequant path on unsupported hardware or if precisions mismatch.
- Added feature flag checks and a runtime self-test path on startup to validate kernel availability.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: extended existing quant unit tests, +5 new files covering scale edge-cases and fused kernel fallbacks.
- Integration: ran k8s smoke tests and bench harness on a dedicated perf node farm (internal perf infra).
- CI: initial run returned a flaky test (tests/quant/quant_fusion_tests.cc::PerChannelScaleEdgeCases) failing on one runner; rerun succeeded. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Performance review notes:
- Benched across NVIDIA A100 and H100 variants; FP8 fast-path requires appropriate compute capability and is skipped on older GPUs.
- For multi-tenant Dedicated clusters, enable_quant_fusion is recommended behind staged rollout to verify tail P99 behavior in the wild.

Release notes:
- Improves throughput and cost for INT8/FP8 quantized inference by introducing fused dequant+GEMM kernels and SmoothQuant folding. Adds KV-cache locality and continuous-batching heuristics to reduce tail latency under long-lived streaming workloads.

Why this is safe to merge: feature-gated, extensive unit/integration coverage, graceful fallbacks. Performance gains verified on internal perf farm and validated by SRE.

release_notes: Introduce fused dequant+GEMM kernels for INT8/FP8 to reduce memory passes.
Fold SmoothQuant scaling into quant pipeline to eliminate extra tensor ops.
KV-cache layout and continuous batching heuristics improved to lower tail latency in streaming workloads.
Feature gated behind runtime flags; enable via runtime config for canary clusters first.
